Design9795 · aluminium winding · conventional winding, fill ≤ 0.40

Summary

Busbar copper against conventional aluminium

The copper reference is Design9795_1 as built: busbar-connected tooth coils, insulated wire fill 0.513, Motor-CAD armature end-winding MLT multiplier 0.7 (mean turn 203.6 mm, 13.48 mΩ per path at 100 °C). Every aluminium design is a conventional winding: insulated wire fill at most 0.40, standard wire sizes, end-winding multiplier 1.136 (end turns 1.623 × longer), and the strands in hand treated as one bundle for proximity loss, as Motor-CAD does with Include Bundle Effect: more strands do not reduce the AC loss. The rotor is unchanged; only the stator, stack length and winding change.

Aluminium can replace the copper winding of Design9795_1 with stator-only changes (rotor cross-section, magnets, air gap and M235-35A kept), and a conventional winding at 40 % fill, but not at equal efficiency up to OD 170. The best balance saves ₹418 per motor (10 % of active-material cost) for 3.73 % range.

Recommended · OD 170 · 86 mm

−₹418

Range -3.73 % (telematics), -3.75 % (WMTC). Stator K6 (OD 170, yoke 7.85 mm, slot 23.65 mm deep, tooth 13.54 mm), 86 mm stack, 8 turns × 3 × 2.12 mm Al. Torque within 0.8 % of copper at every speed, +1.82 kg. Winding loss at peak torque +24 %.

Alternative, 98.5 % torque at high speed · OD 170 · 80 mm

−₹612

Range -3.10 % / -3.32 %. Stator K2 (OD 170, yoke 7.85 mm, slot 23.65 mm deep, tooth 15.54 mm), 80 mm stack, 8 turns × 1 × 3.55 mm Al. Winding loss at peak +28 %, +1.41 kg.

Least range loss · OD 170 · 90 mm

−₹124

Range -3.12 % / -3.38 %. Stator K1 (OD 170, yoke 8.85 mm, slot 22.65 mm deep, tooth 15.54 mm), 90 mm stack, 7 turns × 4 × 1.83 mm Al. Winding loss at peak +13 %, +2.68 kg.

Range parity is not reached: aluminium needs 1.64 × copper's conductor area for the same resistance (about 2.0 × with the longer end turns of the 1.136 multiplier). At 0.40 fill instead of 0.513, the stators up to OD 170 give only 0.78–1.30 × copper's conductor area at the same turns, so fewer turns and longer stacks carry the design. Each OD page has the details: stator variants, all best designs, efficiency maps, OP1–OP3, drive cycle and cost.

Method and copper baseline

Every number comes from the Motor-CAD-equivalent FEMM model of Design9795_1, extended with FEMM solutions of each stator variant, then run through the vehicle drive cycles.

StageScriptWhat it computesCount
1. Copper modellab_model.py (v3), make_lab_v2.pyMotor-CAD-equivalent Lab model: skew slices, Motor-CAD torque, minor-loop hysteresis + harmonic eddy iron lossvalidated on 840 Motor-CAD map points
2. Stator variantsalu9795_femm.py (FEMM)Torque, d-q flux, stator iron-loss sums, slot field, tooth and yoke flux density on a 4 × 4 current grid × 2 rotor positions28 stators × 32 = 896 solves
3. Design searchalu9795_study.py, alu9795_search.pyEach stator × stack 64–100 mm × 7/8/9/10 turns per coil × wire (largest area at fill ≤ 0.40; also the fewest strands within 3 % of it): envelope, efficiency map, peak point, drive cycles, cost2946 designs
4. Best designsalu9795_analyse.pyCost against range fronts per OD and criterion; Al price sensitivity5 ODs × 2 criteria × 3 prices
5. FEMM checkalu9795_verify.pyDirect solves between grid nodes, 4 rotor positions, against the interpolation60 solves
6. Operating pointsalu9795_ops.pyOP1–OP3: currents, phase advance, voltage, flux, power factor, loss breakdown16 designs

Copper baseline (Design9795_1)

Stator OD 160 mm, bore 107 mm, 12 slots, slot depth 17.65 mm, tooth 15.54 mm, yoke 8.85 mm, slot 281.2 mm²; 10-pole spoke ferrite rotor; 64 mm stack; delta, 2 parallel paths, 10 turns per coil of SWG 11 (2.946 mm) copper, fill 0.513; M235-35A. Drive: 52 V, modulation 0.95 (49.4 V phase peak), 360 A rms line, 280 A DC, MTPA. Winding and magnets at 100 °C.

Busbar copper against conventional aluminium

The copper reference is Design9795_1 as built: busbar-connected tooth coils, insulated wire fill 0.513, Motor-CAD armature end-winding MLT multiplier 0.7 (mean turn 203.6 mm, 13.48 mΩ per path at 100 °C). Every aluminium design is a conventional winding: insulated wire fill at most 0.40, standard wire sizes, end-winding multiplier 1.136 (end turns 1.623 × longer), and the strands in hand treated as one bundle for proximity loss, as Motor-CAD does with Include Bundle Effect: more strands do not reduce the AC loss. The rotor is unchanged; only the stator, stack length and winding change.

The FEMM copper model matches Motor-CAD Lab within 0.28 efficiency points (mean over 840 map points), 1.6 % torque and 2.7 % total loss; envelope torque within 0.7 % from 1000 to 9000 rpm (see the Lab validation report).

Motor-CAD values from its envelope export (OP1, OP3). Motor-CAD splits iron loss into stator/rotor and hysteresis/eddy for the machine; its OP1 hysteresis 111 W, eddy 184 W. FEMM's OP1 iron loss is lower (the known hysteresis gap), so copper's FEMM efficiency is +0.46 points against Motor-CAD at OP1 and +0.08 at OP3. Aluminium designs are compared with FEMM copper, so this offset cancels.

How an aluminium design is evaluated

  • Turns: currents scaled by turns (same ampere-turns give the same field), flux linkage × turns, end-winding inductance × turns².
  • Stack length: flux, torque, iron loss and windage scale with length (2D); end-turn length unchanged.
  • Stator variant: FEMM differences against the copper stator at the same ampere-turns, added to the copper model (flux), or as ratios (stator iron loss, slot field). Checked against direct FEMM solves: ψq within 0.88 %, iron-loss ratio within 1.6 %.
  • Winding: aluminium EC-1350 (2.826 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m at 20 °C, 0.00403/K, 2703 kg/m³) at 100 °C; conventional winding with insulated wire fill at most 0.40 (copper's busbar winding: 0.513); standard IEC and SWG wire sizes from 1.0 mm, 1–8 strands; mean turn = 2L + 1.136/0.7 × end turn corrected for tooth width and coil thickness; AC loss by Motor-CAD's hybrid method (factor 2) with FEMM's slot field and the bundle effect: the strands in hand count as one round conductor of the same total area (loss ∝ turns × (strands × d²)²), so it does not fall with more strands.
  • Acceptance: full = peak torque ≥ 99.5 % of copper and envelope ≥ 99 % at every speed 0–9500 rpm; relaxed = envelope ≥ 97 % (shortfall only in the DC-power-limited region above about 3000 rpm).

Design9795 · aluminium winding · conventional winding, fill ≤ 0.40

OD 160 mm

Same OD and housing as copper. The slot can only grow inward (thinner yoke) or sideways (thinner teeth), and both cost torque per ampere-turn: −1.3 % per mm of yoke, −1.9 % per mm of tooth. Aluminium therefore needs a long stack. 723 designs evaluated at this OD; 0 keep full torque at every speed, 120 stay within 3 %.

Comparison across ODs

A larger OD moves the whole cost-range front up and to the right: each mm of OD adds 0.5 mm of slot depth (about 11 mm² per slot) for about 0.06 kg (₹18) of stator steel. That is cheaper than adding stack length, which also lengthens the rotor and magnets.

Design9795 · aluminium winding · conventional winding, fill ≤ 0.40

Drive cycle and range

Range is computed from energy per km at the motor terminals over two speed traces: the telematics log supplied earlier and WMTC Class 1. Range change = copper Wh/km ÷ aluminium Wh/km − 1, counting motor losses only.

Vehicle and method

  • Vehicle (given): GVW 757 kg, CdA 1.117 m², wheel radius 0.30 m, gear ratio 13.9. Assumed: rolling resistance 0.015, gearbox efficiency 0.95, rotating-mass factor 1.05, flat road.
  • Motor torque from road load and acceleration at each 1 s step; regenerative braking down to −26.4 N·m (largest regen torque in the log), friction brakes beyond.
  • Telematics: 10.75 km, 6363 steps (logging gaps skipped), motor up to 6908 rpm, 18 % of steps motoring. WMTC Class 1: 7.67 km, up to 6139 rpm.
  • The logged motor torque is negative even at cruise, so energy is computed from the speed trace through the vehicle model, not from the logged torque.
  • Losses are read from each design's own loss map (MTPA) at the cycle's speed and torque; points above a design's torque limit are held at the limit.
  • Inverter, battery and vehicle are the same for every design, so the battery-level range change is about the motor-level change.

Where the range goes

  • The cycles run mostly at light and medium torque below 6000 rpm. There, aluminium's higher DC resistance and the longer stacks' extra iron loss outweigh its lower AC loss.
  • Copper's AC winding loss over the telematics cycle is 0.84 Wh/km; aluminium's is 0.58 Wh/km (recommended, bundle effect), but its DC loss rises from 2.82 to 3.46 Wh/km and iron loss from 3.04 to 4.75 Wh/km.
  • Each 1 % of range is about 0.61 Wh/km at the motor. Battery capacity was not given, so the battery cost of making up the range is not included.

  • Longer stacks add stator steel, rotor laminations and magnets: about ₹41–43 per mm of stack. A larger OD adds only stator steel, about ₹18 per mm of OD.
  • Lamination cost is on net mass (stator + rotor). The larger blank of a larger OD (gross 12.77 → 19.32 kg for the recommended design) is not included, nor are the die, housing, terminations and winding process.
  • Copper's active-material cost is ₹4349: wire ₹1719, laminations ₹1526, magnets ₹1104.

Stator lamination
OD 160 → 170 mm. Slot depth 17.65 → 23.65 mm (slot bottom radius 71.15 → 77.15 mm). Yoke 8.85 → 7.85 mm. Tooth 15.54 → 13.54 mm. Unchanged: bore 107 mm, 12 slots, tooth tip, slot opening, slot-bottom corner radius, M235-35A 0.35 mm. Slot area 281.2 → 462.1 mm². New lamination die and housing bore.
Stack length
64 → 86 mm for stator, rotor laminations and magnets (same cross-sections). Shaft, bearing span and housing +22 mm.
Winding
Aluminium EC-1350, grade-2 enamel, 3 strands in hand × 2.12 mm (about 2.19 mm over enamel), 8 turns per coil, delta, 2 parallel paths, one coil per tooth, needle- or flyer-wound with continuous inter-coil connections (no busbar). Insulated wire fill 0.392 (limit 0.40; copper busbar winding 0.513). Mean turn 297.1 mm; 16.78 mΩ per path at 100 °C (copper 13.48).
Terminations
Only the phase-path ends are joined: 3 strands per end, ultrasonic or laser welded to an aluminium lead or a friction-welded Al-Cu terminal (no soldering), sealed against galvanic corrosion.
Drive
Same limits. New flux and resistance tables in the controller (flux and torque per amp ×1.075 against copper: stack × turns); aluminium temperature coefficient 0.00403/K.

Design9795 · aluminium winding · conventional winding, fill ≤ 0.40

Assumptions and files

Limits of the study

  • 2D FEA; end effects only through the end-turn resistance and end-winding inductance.
  • Thermal behaviour not simulated; the higher winding loss at peak torque needs a Motor-CAD thermal check.
  • Aluminium insulated wire fill held at or below 0.40 (conventional winding); the real fill depends on the winding process and should be measured on trial coils.
  • AC loss by the low-frequency hybrid method with the bundle effect, as Motor-CAD; when the equivalent bundle diameter (√strands × d) exceeds the skin depth (about 2.6 mm hot copper, 3.3 mm aluminium at 750 Hz) it overestimates the loss, so the aluminium figures are on the safe side.
  • Flux maps, demagnetisation, torque ripple and THD were not recomputed for these stator-only variants: the rotor is unchanged, and the slot opening and tooth tip are identical to copper's.
  • Costs are active materials only.
